newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican guerrillas warn Paris of further attacks.
newsitem.headline: Corsican guerrillas warn Paris of further attacks.

text.p: A banned Corsican separatist group warned France's new leftist government on Wednesday it would keep up its violent campaign for autonomy from Paris if it did not win concessions.

The FLNC (Corsican National Liberation Front) announced at a late night news conference in the northern mountains of the Mediterranean island that it was "ready to cross swords with all enemies of the Corsican nation".
The warning was made by a group of seven armed and hooded men in military fatigues who asked Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to "clarify his position".
They reiterated the group's principal demands, including autonomy from Paris, teaching of the Corsican language in schools, and electoral and political reform.
The FLNC was created in 1996 by dissident members of two other separatist guerrilla groups.

One of them, the FLNC Historic Wing, announced last month it had suspended its armed struggle to give Jospin's government, which unseated the previous right-wing majority in parliamentary elections last month, time to set its policy.

Separatist guerrillas have claimed responsibility for hundreds of bombings in their two-decade campaign for greater autonomy from the mainland. Most of them were aimed at government buildings symbolising authority like law courts or post offices.
